reason: Redesign the Taskboard factory UI as a cohesive software-factory operator console. The current ticket detail is an unstructured vertical dump with duplicate status, legacy-session emphasis, weak hierarchy, and excessive scrolling. Create a new whole-page layout that prioritizes ticket identity and controls, a clear coordinator and child-agent team, a compact phase pipeline, current blockers and active work, and drill-down evidence. Preserve existing behavior, accessibility, mobile responsiveness, BB design conventions, factory recovery controls, and provider-backed status. Prototype multiple structurally distinct layouts, choose the strongest through browser evidence, implement it, and verify desktop and mobile in the live BB surface.
spec:
# Build An Autonomous Software Factory Into The Existing Taskboard Plugin

## Request

> Build an autonomous software factory into the existing Taskboard plugin, inspired by https://github.com/lpbaril/bb-plugin-factory. Make Linear, Jira, or the configured issue provider the source of truth. The factory should continuously select eligible tickets, start and supervise BB agent work, avoid duplicate dispatch, recover after restart, and reflect progress back through the existing Taskboard provider/status model. Reuse the current taskboard architecture and keep the first implementation focused and operable.

## Goal

An explicitly enabled project factory continuously admits eligible tickets from
the project's configured issue provider and runs the existing investigation,
planning, isolated build, independent review, and bounded repair workflow. Each
admitted ticket has one visible coordinator thread. The stage agents appear as
children of that coordinator, so users can inspect the ticket team as one group
without requiring a person to press Start task on each ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [AC-1] Factories are disabled by default. Project-scoped settings persist an explicit enable choice, provider identity, intake policy, and bounded concurrency.
- [ ] [AC-2] Enabled factories discover provider todo tickets, exclude durable claims before applying the bounded scan window, revalidate live eligibility before dispatch, and admit eligible tickets without a manual per-ticket action. Backlog, closed, canceled, previously claimed, and wrong-provider tickets are not admitted.
- [ ] [AC-3] Concurrent ticks and plugin restart cannot duplicate an admitted ticket, its coordinator, or a stage agent, and cannot exceed the configured autonomous workflow capacity. Ambiguous native dispatch remains blocked rather than retried.
- [ ] [AC-4] Each automatically admitted ticket has exactly one visible coordinator thread. Investigation, planning, Build, Review, and bounded repair sessions are native child threads of that coordinator. Build still uses a managed worktree, Review stays independent, native execution defaults remain in effect, and existing manual starts continue to work.
- [ ] [AC-5] Pausing stops automatic admission and subsequent automatic stage dispatch for queue-owned work while preserving active native threads and observed progress. Provider changes, missing configuration, failed live reads, stale eligibility, scope changes, and closure changes fail closed. Project Manage and the affected ticket group show a short operator-readable state and reason; no action dispatches from stale data.
- [ ] [AC-6] Provider progress updates remain explicit observations. No new action merges, deploys, or closes an issue; a passed review remains awaiting human acceptance. Ticket scope and closure changes prevent subsequent automatic dispatch.
- [ ] [AC-7] CLI and RPC expose project factory settings and status with validation. Project status includes queue-owned workflow blockers even after a healthy provider scan. Focused behavioral tests cover duplicate ticks, restart, capacity, pause, scan-window fairness, stale provider data, hierarchy recovery, and failure isolation.
- [ ] [AC-UI-1] [UI] Project Manage exposes persisted enablement, provider identity, intake policy, bounded concurrency, pause/resume, queue and active counts, last scan result, and blockers using existing Taskboard components. Healthy idle, paused, missing-configuration, and provider-error states are distinct. Ticket progress shows the coordinator and grouped stage agents with role, native state, a direct thread action, and operator-readable blockers above the group. Long titles, provider names, and reasons remain readable without horizontal overflow. Disclosure and thread actions are keyboard accessible with visible focus; expanded groups remain stable across data refresh. Desktop and mobile browser evidence covers these states.

## Scope

Taskboard factory contracts, persistence, native thread hierarchy, orchestration,
server integration, CLI, project Manage controls, ticket progress, focused
tests, browser fixture, and related README.

## Non-goals

No new issue provider, credential system, independent local task tracker,
unrestricted permission mode, automatic merge/deployment, PR lifecycle, or claim
of independently verified completion. No automatic enablement of live projects.
The first version coordinates one BB installation, not distributed claims across
independent BB servers sharing the same tracker. The coordinator does not plan,
write code, review, or own a second workflow state machine. It is the stable
native parent and user entry point for the stage agents.

## Risks

Native dispatch may succeed before its response is lost. Preserve the existing
uncertain state and human recovery path. Provider reads and local claims are not
one transaction, so revalidate live input and persist the claim before dispatch.
An active native thread is not forcibly canceled when intake is paused or ticket
scope changes. Use the native Stop control for that operation. Creating the
coordinator is also a native dispatch. Persist its starting intent first, and
never create a replacement after an ambiguous outcome. Existing records without
a coordinator remain readable and gain one only through an explicit, idempotent
recovery path.

## Verification

Run focused controller and store tests with real SQLite and mocked external SDK
boundaries, then the Taskboard check from the workspace root. Exercise factory
settings in the existing browser fixture at desktop and mobile sizes and inspect
screenshots. Prove that one coordinator owns every new stage child, that restart
does not duplicate either level, and that a missing or ambiguous coordinator
blocks automatic dispatch. Run the existing opt-in read-only native smoke where
BB context is available. Do not enable a live tracker queue as a test.

Browser evidence must cover Project Manage in healthy idle, paused, missing
configuration, and provider-error states, plus ticket groups blocked by stale
eligibility, scope change, and closure change. Check long titles, provider names,
and blocker reasons at narrow widths. Exercise keyboard disclosure and thread
actions, visible focus, and expanded-state retention across data refresh.

## Capability Deltas

Create one or more files under deltas/<capability>.md using ADDED, MODIFIED, or
REMOVED Requirements sections, named Requirement blocks, and concrete Scenario
examples. These merge into living specifications
after verification and review.

deltas.purpose:
Admit ready provider tickets into Taskboard's durable native-agent workflow
without per-ticket manual starts, while keeping capacity, recovery, and human
acceptance boundaries explicit.

requirements.name: Explicit project factory admission
requirements.contents:
### Requirement: Explicit project factory admission

The factory MUST remain disabled until explicitly enabled for a project's
selected issue provider. It MUST discover eligible todo tickets and persist
admission before starting a native worker.

#### Scenario: An enabled project receives a ready ticket

- GIVEN a configured provider and an enabled project factory with capacity
- WHEN a previously unclaimed ticket is eligible in the live provider
- THEN Taskboard starts its investigation without a per-ticket click
- AND records the ticket identity before native dispatch.

#### Scenario: Duplicate admission and restart

- GIVEN a ticket with a durable factory claim
- WHEN concurrent ticks or a restarted service discover that ticket
- THEN no second workflow is admitted
- AND an uncertain dispatch is never automatically retried.

#### Scenario: Claimed tickets fill the first provider page

- GIVEN more cached todo tickets than one bounded intake scan can inspect
- AND the first tickets already have durable claims
- WHEN the factory has available capacity
- THEN Taskboard excludes those claims before it applies the scan limit
- AND later eligible tickets can still be admitted.

requirements.name: One coordinator per ticket team
requirements.contents:
### Requirement: One coordinator per ticket team

Each automatically admitted ticket MUST own one visible native coordinator
thread. Every new Investigation, Plan, Build, and Review session for that ticket
MUST be a native child of the coordinator. The existing factory record remains
the only workflow state machine.

#### Scenario: A ticket starts its agent team

- GIVEN a newly admitted ticket without a coordinator
- WHEN automatic work starts
- THEN Taskboard persists coordinator dispatch intent before the native call
- AND creates one visible coordinator thread
- AND creates the Investigation session as its child.

#### Scenario: Later stages and repair

- GIVEN a ticket with a linked coordinator
- WHEN planning, Build, Review, or a repair session starts
- THEN each new native session has the coordinator as its parent
- AND Build continuations still reuse the original Build child and worktree.

#### Scenario: Coordinator dispatch is ambiguous

- GIVEN Taskboard cannot prove whether the coordinator was created
- WHEN the service restarts or scans the ticket again
- THEN it does not create another coordinator or stage session
- AND it exposes a recovery action to link the existing native thread.

#### Scenario: Existing manual workflow

- GIVEN a manual factory record created before ticket coordinators existed
- WHEN a user inspects or continues that record
- THEN its existing runs remain readable and recoverable
- AND Taskboard does not silently reparent existing native threads.

requirements.name: Bounded and observable automation
requirements.contents:
### Requirement: Bounded and observable automation

The factory MUST enforce its autonomous workflow capacity in code and expose
project settings and status through RPC, CLI, and project Manage.

#### Scenario: Pause during work

- GIVEN an enabled factory with a running native thread
- WHEN the operator pauses the factory
- THEN the thread remains visible and is not forcibly stopped
- AND no new queue-owned stage or ticket starts until resumed.

#### Scenario: Provider truth cannot be established

- GIVEN a factory bound to one provider configuration
- WHEN the provider changes or a live read fails
- THEN automatic dispatch stops with an observable error
- AND cached eligibility alone does not authorize a new dispatch.

#### Scenario: One workflow is blocked after a healthy scan

- GIVEN provider candidate discovery succeeds
- AND a queue-owned ticket cannot complete a required live read
- WHEN the operator checks project factory status
- THEN the status reports blocked work and its reason
- AND the successful scan does not hide that workflow failure.

#### Scenario: Operator distinguishes idle, paused, and failed

- GIVEN an operator opens Project Manage
- WHEN the factory is healthy and idle, intentionally paused, missing required
  configuration, or blocked by a provider read failure
- THEN Taskboard shows a distinct state label and short reason
- AND shows persisted enablement, provider identity, intake policy, concurrency,
  queue and active counts, and last scan result
- AND cached counts are labeled as last known rather than current eligibility.

requirements.name: Preserve execution and acceptance boundaries
requirements.contents:
### Requirement: Preserve execution and acceptance boundaries

Queue-owned tickets MUST reuse the existing managed build and independent review
workflow. Automatic processing MUST NOT merge, deploy, or close tracker tickets.

#### Scenario: Review passes

- GIVEN an implemented build and an independent passed review
- WHEN reconciliation observes the result
- THEN work remains awaiting human acceptance
- AND the ticket is not automatically closed.

#### Scenario: Ticket scope changes or closes

- GIVEN an automatically admitted ticket
- WHEN a live provider read reports changed scope or a terminal status
- THEN no subsequent automatic stage starts from the stale plan
- AND the ticket shows `Scope changed` or `Ticket closed` above its team with a
  short reason and no action that bypasses the blocker.

#### Scenario: Cached eligibility is unconfirmed

- GIVEN a queue-owned ticket was previously eligible
- WHEN a required live provider read fails
- THEN subsequent automatic dispatch remains blocked
- AND the ticket shows `Provider status stale` and the live-read reason above
  its team
- AND existing native threads remain openable
- AND no recovery action authorizes dispatch from cached eligibility.

requirements.name: Visible ticket team hierarchy
requirements.contents:
### Requirement: Visible ticket team hierarchy

Taskboard MUST show the coordinator and its stage children as one ticket team.
Each row MUST show the role, current native state, and an action that opens the
native thread. The grouping MUST remain readable on desktop and mobile.

#### Scenario: Inspect an active ticket

- GIVEN a ticket with a coordinator and three stage sessions
- WHEN the user opens factory progress
- THEN one coordinator row contains the Investigation, Plan, and Build rows
- AND each row opens its exact native thread.

#### Scenario: Inspect on a narrow viewport

- GIVEN a mobile viewport
- WHEN the user opens factory progress
- THEN role and state remain visible
- AND actions remain reachable
- AND the page has no horizontal overflow.

#### Scenario: Long operator-facing content

- GIVEN a long ticket title, provider name, or blocker reason
- WHEN Project Manage or factory progress is viewed on a narrow viewport
- THEN titles and reasons wrap to readable lines
- AND provider identity wraps without obscuring controls
- AND role, native state, and actions retain readable rows
- AND the page has no horizontal overflow.

#### Scenario: Keyboard and refresh behavior

- GIVEN a user navigates factory progress by keyboard
- WHEN focus reaches a ticket disclosure or `Open thread` action
- THEN the control has a visible focus indicator and activates with its
  platform-standard keyboard action
- AND the disclosure exposes its expanded state to assistive technology
- AND a user-expanded or collapsed group retains that state across data refresh
  while that ticket remains present.
